text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
- Budapest welcomes the EU's recommendation that the EU initiate accession negotiations with Hungary and five other countries, Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs told a news conference.
- Hungary's economic stabilisation policy had brought results by the end of 1996 and early 1997, head of department at the Ministry of Finace, Tamas Tetenyisaid.

- The senior coalition member Socialist Party (MSZP) is looking for campaign allies as the 1998 elections approach but neither of the two leading parties, the Young Democrats and the Smallhalders, in the parliamentary opposition are likely to pass muster, a top MSZP official told a news conference after a meeting of the party's national presidium on Wednesday.
- Police cannot secretly videotape public roads for reasons unrelated to specific criminal investigations, Laszlo Majtenyi, commissioner for data protection, sayd Wednesday.
- Real wages grew an average of 23.8 percent in January-May, while net wages increased 26.4 percent, the Central Statistical Office said.
- The state privatisation agency APV Rt has awarded the 9.61 percent or one billion forint face value stake on offer in K&H Bank to the consortium of Kredietbank and Irish Life.
- The Suzuki Motor Corp and the Japanese trading house Itochu have increaed their respective stakes in Magyar Suzuki Rt.

- The government has long failed to fulfill its oblligation to control the monopoly of the Hungarian Telecommunications Co (MATAV) to the detriment of many thousands of telephone users, an MP of the oppositon Democratic Forum said at the party's press conference (MAGYAR NEMZET too).

- As part of an earlier compensation agreement between the Hungarian government and the World Jewish Congress, Hungary will extend 480 million forints in collective repaarations to Roma victims of the Holocaust in Hungary and their dependents, a government offical announced.

- Although the economy has reached a stage of permanent growth, the boom must not be allowed to overaccelerate and bring with it the macroeconomic disturbances of previous years, Minister of Industry and Trade Szabolcs Fazakaes told representatives of foreign ambassies on Wednesday.

- The state privatisation agency APV Rt received revenues of 120 billion from privatisation in the first half of this year, and a further 10 billion forint is soon expected to flow in, chairman of the APV board of directors Arpad Kovacs said.
- Three commercial banks have cut lending rates from July 14.
